title: feat(spec,objectql): declare the masked-on-read field types in spec; collectMaskedReadFields derives (#20141)
body:
Fixes #20141
Clause-②: yes

## What

`packages/spec/src/data/masked-field-types.ts` declares, once, which field types are masked on read (ADR-0100). It is re-exported from `@objectstack/spec/data`, beside `secret-mask`:

- `MASKED_ON_READ_FIELD_TYPES`: a deep-frozen per-type rule table. `secret` has `exemptManagedBy: []`, so it is masked on every object. `password` has `exemptManagedBy: ['better-auth']`.
- `isMaskedOnReadFieldType(fieldType, managedBy)`: the one reading of that table.
- `FieldTypeReadMask`: the rule's type. Its `exemptManagedBy` is typed against `ObjectSchema.managedBy`'s own enum.

The `FieldType` prose for `password` / `secret` (`field.zod.ts`, the enum comments only) now cites the declaration. It used to be the only statement of the fact.

In `@objectstack/objectql`, `collectMaskedReadFields` and its sibling `collectMaskedPasswordFields` now ask `isMaskedOnReadFieldType`. They no longer carry their own `def.type === 'secret'` / `'password'` arms or their own `managedBy === 'better-auth'` test. **No behaviour change.** The evidence is below.

## Why a per-type rule plus a predicate (the AI-misuse axis)

- **An exemption cannot be separated from its type.** Suppose the shape were a bare type set with a separate exemption map. A reader could take the set and drop the map, which masks `password` on better-auth objects and breaks login. Or it could take the map without the set. Here the exemption is a field of the rule it qualifies.
- **Exemptions fail closed.** The list names the buckets that are NOT masked. Any `managedBy` the table does not list exempts nothing: `undefined`, a future bucket, a typo in stored unvalidated metadata. So the field stays masked. An allow-list ("masked when managedBy is ...") would unmask on exactly those inputs.
- **Nothing can be invented.** Keys are checked against `FieldType`, and exemption values against `ObjectSchema.managedBy`'s enum, at compile time. The reverse verification below shows both refusals. The spec test holds the same two memberships at run time against the live schemas.
- **`managedBy` is a required argument** of the predicate. A call site cannot leave the exemption out by omission. It passes `undefined` explicitly for an object with no bucket.
- Rejected: a per-field flag on `FieldSchema`. That would be a new authorable key an author could set or unset per field, not a fact about the type.

No new `managedBy` value is introduced, and the predicate reads no key the spec does not declare.

## The sibling collector

`collectMaskedPasswordFields` (the password scope of the empty-credential refusal) derives too. It keeps its `'password'` arm, because that is its scope by definition, not a copy of the masked set. It asks the predicate for the exemption.

`collectCredentialFields` and `collectSecretFields` answer different questions and are untouched (see Acceptance notes). The first is the aggregate refusal: `secret` or `password`, unconditionally. The second is the encryption write path.

## Security floor: masked-on-read answer identical to `main`

I ran one table through `main`'s `collectMaskedReadFields` / `collectMaskedPasswordFields` (base `4df101c38`, file blob `708318ed6`) and through this branch's (blob `86b21b30f`). Each row records both collectors' answers.

The rows cover every `FieldType` (49 types) plus 10 off-enum `type` inputs. They include non-strings, `['secret']`, `'constructor'`, `'toString'`, `'__proto__'` and case variants. Each type is crossed with 11 `managedBy` inputs: key absent, the six declared buckets, `undefined`, `null`, the retired `'system'`, and `'not-a-bucket'`. With one mixed object per `managedBy` and 5 degenerate schemas, that is 665 rows. sha256 of the JSON:

| collector | masked cells | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| base `4df101c38` | 21 | `8a418a2e1b6ed2a6159f5b1e6289d25703df5c0d8eacd3e151084a96bcdc5fd7` |
| this branch | 21 | `8a418a2e1b6ed2a6159f5b1e6289d25703df5c0d8eacd3e151084a96bcdc5fd7` |
| control: base with the `secret` arm deleted | 10 | `0cdcbcad7818e65526687c0bd8e6dd09a60bb54a6b3dfbe040ce8652358cc216` |

The control row shows the harness tells the two apart.

Three in-repo pins were added to `packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.test.ts`, over the same `FieldType` x `managedBy` population:

- **The floor:** a literal expected column (secret always, password unless better-auth, nothing else). It does not read the spec, so any edit to the declaration turns it red and has to be read.
- **The agreement:** the runtime collectors and the spec predicate give the same answer, cell for cell.
- **Order:** a mixed-object pin on order and empty definitions.

`packages/spec/src/data/masked-field-types.test.ts` pins the table's content, its vocabulary against the live enums, the deep freeze and the predicate over the full grid.

## Ablation (committed first, restored and proven)

With `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, I pointed `collectMaskedReadFields` back at a hard-coded copy that drops `secret`: `def.type === 'password'` and managedBy is not better-auth. The mutation landed (anchor 1 to 0; blob `86b21b30f` to `0533a577a`).

`vitest run src/secret-fields.test.ts` then reported **6 failed | 34 passed**:

- the agreement pin: `"secret" x (absent): expected false to be true`
- the floor
- the mixed-object pin
- three existing secret masking tests

Restored with `git checkout HEAD`: blob equals HEAD `86b21b30f`, `git diff HEAD` is empty, status is clean. The subject is imported relatively (`./secret-fields.js`, i.e. `src`), so no `dist` sits on the resolution path.

## Reverse verification (the declaration's types)

Run with `tsc --noEmit -p packages/spec/tsconfig.json` against the mutated file, then restored (blob `38b1cadb6`, `git diff HEAD` empty):

- An invented `managedBy` value (`['better-auth', 'identity']`): **tsc exit 2**, TS2322 at `masked-field-types.ts(90,14)` and `(98,5)`.
- An invented key (`pin_code`): **tsc exit 2**, TS2353 "Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'pin_code' does not exist" at `(94,5)`.
- My first attempt at the key leg was a no-op. The replacement contained its own anchor, and `ablation-replace` refused it and restored. It was rerun with a disjoint anchor.

## Tests (at `3d14f9e75`, after merging `main` `805af4f29`)

All runs are `--project local` where the package has projects:

| package | test files | tests | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` | 545 | 16041 (+2 todo) | passed |
| `@objectstack/objectql` | 318 | 5766 | passed |
| `@objectstack/platform-objects` | 55 | 911 | passed |
| `@objectstack/plugin-audit` | 25 | 363 | passed |

`plugin-audit` imports `collectMaskedReadFields` from `@objectstack/objectql/core` in `audit-writers.ts`; this consumer was missing from the dispatch list.

Typecheck: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` exit 0, and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` exit 0. `--listFilesOnly` confirms both new or edited test files are in the test tsc programs.

## Gates (at `3d14f9e75`)

- **Dispatch gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 87 commands, and `--ran` reconciled them: **85 run, all exit 0; 2 NOT MEASURED; 0 unrun.**
- **NOT MEASURED.** `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:type-check-debt` both exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). Each needs every workspace package's `dist`, and only the spec to objectql closure is built here. CI builds the whole tree.
- **Regenerated artifacts.** `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` were regenerated, not hand-edited. They add 3 entries each; everything else is untouched.
- **Narrowed lint** (not the repo-wide `pnpm lint`): `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 6 changed TS files gave 6 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. eslint's own config reports each file as linted, not ignored. `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move a verdict in an untouched file.

## For objectui (no objectui change here)

objectui's `MASKED_FIELD_TYPES` / `isMaskedFieldType()` in `@object-ui/fields` should re-bind, on its own card once a spec release carrying this is installable, to **`isMaskedOnReadFieldType`** from `@objectstack/spec/data`. It should pass the object's `managedBy`.

If the renderer must enumerate the masked types, `Object.keys(MASKED_ON_READ_FIELD_TYPES)` is the set. It should still ask the predicate for the exemption rather than restate it.

Whether the renderer honours the better-auth exemption is that card's decision. No shipped better-auth object declares a `password`-typed field today (`platform-objects.test.ts` pins that).

## Acceptance notes

These are not filed.

- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` `warnGenericPasswordFields` (the author-time warning) keeps its own `managedBy === 'better-auth'` / `type === 'password'` test. That is a third spelling of the password half of this fact, inside spec. It agrees today and is outside this card's file surface. Deriving it from `isMaskedOnReadFieldType` is a mechanical follow-up for whoever next edits that function.
- ADR-0100 section C names `collectMaskedReadFields` as "the one place" the better-auth exemption lives. After this PR the one place is the spec declaration and the collector derives, which is the same single-ownership decision relocated. The ADR text is Tier H and outside this surface, so a status-line or pointer amendment is the maintainer's call.
- `collectCredentialFields` (the aggregate refusal set, `secret` or `password` unconditionally) is a separate hand-written type list by design ("is this a credential type?"). If the masked set ever grows, the aggregate refusal will not follow on its own. That drift has not been exercised; no card.
